document_purpose: Compiled, source-verified vehicle class comparison for Can It Ford, built from live Scite and web research on 2026-07-21. This is NOT a live NHTSA vPIC pull. Curb weight and precise vPIC fields for the RAV4 and CR-V still need to be pulled separately, either via a real VIN decode or manufacturer spec sheets.

small_passenger.source: Ball et al. 2019, ARR Book 6, and Shand, Cox, Blacka & Smith 2011, AR&R Report P10/S2/020

large_4wd.source: Ball et al. 2019, ARR Book 6, and Shand, Cox, Blacka & Smith 2011, AR&R Report P10/S2/020

large_passenger_or_crossover.ar_and_r_class: large passenger (approximate mapping, mid-size SUV, not a strict AR&R sedan)
large_passenger_or_crossover.source: Ball et al. 2019, ARR Book 6, and Shand, Cox, Blacka & Smith 2011, AR&R Report P10/S2/020
large_passenger_or_crossover.note: Explorer is mid-size, not a strict AR&R large passenger sedan, mapping is approximate

proposed_fourth_class.category: small footprint, high ground clearance (compact SUV/crossover)
proposed_fourth_class.rationale: AR&R's three classes do not separately distinguish a small-footprint vehicle with SUV-class ground clearance from a small-footprint vehicle with low ground clearance. Buoyancy-versus-submersion-depth behavior differs meaningfully between the two even at similar mass and length.
proposed_fourth_class.era_note: Both existed as real production vehicles by 1998, matching the model year of the three existing project vehicles
proposed_fourth_class.status: Not yet pulled from NHTSA vPIC live. Curb weight and vPIC fields still needed.

historical_test_vehicles_behind_ar_and_r.source: Keller and Mitsch 1993, cited as one of three foundational studies (with Bonham and Hattersley 1967 and Gordon and Stone 1973) underlying the current AR&R vehicle hazard guidelines
historical_test_vehicles_behind_ar_and_r.confirmed_via: Direct citation snippet from Shah, Mustaffa & Martínez 2019, DOI 10.1080/15715124.2019.1566240, via Scite live search 2026-07-21

yaris_mesh_independent_grounding.note: The project's existing Yaris mesh choice is independently grounded, not arbitrary
yaris_mesh_independent_grounding.source: Azhar, Pauwels & Bui 2023, DOI 10.1111/jfr3.12885, used a 1:14 scale Toyota Yaris as its own confirmatory test vehicle
yaris_mesh_independent_grounding.relevance: This is the same paper the project's coup_friction=0.55 value traces to, still flagged UNRESOLVED for the exact numeral

moving_vehicle_literature_confirmed_2026.citation: Shah, Mustaffa & Kim 2018, Instability Criteria for Vehicles in Motion Exposed to Flood Risks
moving_vehicle_literature_confirmed_2026.relevance: First experimental study of a moving vehicle in floodwater, 1:10 scale, force decomposition into buoyancy, drag, friction, and driving force

moving_vehicle_literature_confirmed_2026.citation: Shah, Mustaffa & Martinez 2019, Criterion of vehicle instability in floodwaters: past, present and future
Shah, Mustaffa & Martinez-Gomariz 2019, A review of safety guidelines for vehicles in floodwaters

recent_synthesis_reference.citation: A New Semi-Empirical Model to Predict Vehicle Instability in Urban Flooding
recent_synthesis_reference.note: Calibrates separate stability curves for multiple vehicle categories from a large experimental dataset, confirms AR&R depth thresholds of 0.3/0.4/0.5m and DV thresholds of 0.30/0.45/0.60 m2/s
